Base directory for this skill: /Users/smaschek/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/7.0.2/skills/brainstorming

# Brainstorming

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

Before you start implementing, you must, in order:

1. Lay out the approaches in a message of their own, and have your
   human partner pick one (see Lay out the approaches).
2. Write the design doc, short or full (see Size the Work).
3. Get their approval of that doc.
4. Invoke the superpowers:writing-plans skill.

If nothing is open when you write your first message and there's one
sensible way, steps 1 to 3 happen in that message (see Your First
Message).

Two things aren't implementing: a spike they said yes to (see Spike to
feel things out), and doing what they asked once they've opted out of
the questions.

## Look Before You Ask

In an existing project, or when they've given you context (a spec, a plan,
a handoff, files they pointed at, earlier conversation), dig in before your
first message. Read what they referred to and the code or material it
connects to, and keep reading until you can explain how the relevant
parts work today and what this change would touch. Never ask what the
project or their context already answers, or reopen what they've
already decided.

## Your First Message

Move the work forward, with one of these:

- **They've already said what they want** (a spec, a plan, a detailed
  request): aim for about 200 words for the whole message. Echo their
  request back in your own words, so they can see whether you've got its
  shape: what they want, who it's for, and why, as far as they've said.
  Add what you found that bears on it: how the relevant parts work today
  and what the change would touch. If you found something they may not
  have considered that would change what they're asking for or how it
  has to be built, like a constraint, a conflict, or a cheaper path, say
  so plainly. How to build it comes later, once you understand what they
  want (see Lay out the approaches). End with one line inviting
  corrections. Then, if they haven't told you why they want it, even if
  you can guess, ask about that: one open question in their own terms,
  with nothing to pick from. If they have told you, and their request
  and the project leave open something whose answer would change what
  gets built, ask about the one that would change it most; when its
  choices can be named, sketch each concretely, with what it trades off
  and which you'd pick. If nothing like that is open, there's one
  sensible way: end with the short design itself (the approach, a line on
  why the others don't fit, and the design in a few lines) and ask them
  to approve it. Their approval covers the approach and the design: write
  the short design doc as approved and go on to the plan.
  Specs are often incomplete, so confirm before you build on one.
- **They haven't:** one open question, in their own terms, about the
  biggest thing their request leaves unsettled. Say why you're asking:
  what the answer would change about what you build. For "a website for
  my bakery": "If it's mostly for people deciding whether to stop by,
  I'd lead with hours and what's in the case today; taking orders is a
  different site. What do you want someone to do when they land on it?"

How the message ends depends on whether their message asked for
brainstorming:

- **They asked for it** (by name, by invoking it, or by asking for a
  design discussion): end there. They want this conversation.
- **They didn't:** they may not want a conversation at all. End with a
  light, one-line offer to just get going instead, like
  "Or if you'd rather I just dive in, say so." If they take you up on
  it, this skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
  (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
  asked through the normal workflow.

That's the whole message.

## The Conversation

Ask a question only when the answer would change what gets built and
neither the request nor the project answers it. Otherwise, state your
call and your reason as a proposal they can correct, and move the work
forward. Process steps are always your calls: writing things up, where
files go, looking further, how to show something. Do them and say so.
Ask one at a time. Use plain language, pitched just a little above where
your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use process jargon.
You never need to quote this skill to your human partner.

Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
the rest.

**Get them describing.** Until you know why they want it, ask open
questions, with no example answers attached. Their own words carry
intent that your options can't. Once you know why, when a decision has
choices you can name, sketch each concretely, with what it trades off
and which you'd pick. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?",
propose something concrete.

**How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Read from how they
talk which of those choices they want to make. Someone who raises the how
or asks about trade-offs wants the options with your pick. Someone who
talks about outcomes is handing you the how: make those calls and state
each in a line. When there's existing work, build on what it already
uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
something they agreed to.

**Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
out as questions:

- what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
- why now, and what success looks like to them
- goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
  if it technically works)
- prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
- current state: what exists now, what they've tried
- the details they care about

**Make every question specific** to their project and what they've told
you. Ask Socratically, the way a sharp colleague would: build each
question on their last answer or on something you found, so it helps
them think through a consequence or a case they may have missed
("Voting closes before the meeting, and two members joined this month.
Does someone who joins mid-round get a vote?"). When the reason isn't
already plain, say what you're hoping to learn or what the answer would
change. A proposal they can correct, plus your reason for it, often
beats a question.

**Do recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking further
would help, go look: deeper into their codebase or project, their own

content.text:
I paused before the design because I need a live AWS session to test what Converse accepts.

**The bug.** When `tool_choice` is `ToolChoice::None`, `build_request` sends no `toolConfig` at all (`translate/mod.rs:216-230`). If the history already holds `toolUse` or `toolResult` blocks, Converse rejects the request with the B15 error. The usual case is a final "answer now, no tools" turn after a tool loop.

**What else I found:**
- The native path (`translate/native.rs:70-100`) has the same problem. It removes the user tools for `None`, so it sends no `toolConfig` either. The exception is the structured-output anchor case, where it adds an anchor tool. That case is SMA-847, so it is out of scope here.
- Converse has no `none` tool choice. Each fix either removes the tool blocks from the history, or sends tools and must still stop the model from calling one.

**Candidate approaches, not yet tested:**
1. **Write the tool history as text.** When the choice is `None`, change the `toolUse` and `toolResult` blocks to plain text and send no `toolConfig`. The model cannot call a tool, because it has none. The cost: the model sees a text copy of the tool calls, and it can copy that text pattern in its answer.
2. **Use the Anthropic `tool_choice: none` for Claude.** Send `toolConfig` with the tools, plus `additionalModelRequestFields: {"tool_choice": {"type": "none"}}`. This works only if Bedrock passes the field through, and only for Claude.
3. **Send the tools with no `toolChoice`.** I reject this one, because the model can still call a tool. That breaks "must not call".

I want to probe 1 and 2 on Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5, and also test a `toolConfig` with an empty tool list. The SSO token for `maip-dev-admin` has expired, so please run:

```
! aws sso login --profile maip-dev-admin
```

Before I pick: does a Claude-only fix (approach 2) meet your need, or must `None` work on every Bedrock model family? Approach 1 works on all families.

The probes are complete (us-east-1, 2026-11-21). These are the results.

**Probe results** (all with a `get_weather` tool round in the history):

| Request | Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5 | Nova 2 Lite |
|---|---|---|
| No `toolConfig` (today's `None`) | 400, B15 error | 400, B15 error |
| `toolConfig` with an empty tool list | 400 "request is not valid" | - |
| Tools, no `toolChoice` | **real tool call** | **real tool call** |
| Tools + `additionalModelRequestFields: {"tool_choice":{"type":"none"}}` | 200, no tool call (Converse and ConverseStream) | 400 "extraneous key [tool_choice]" |
| History written as text, no `toolConfig` | 200, no tool call | 200, no tool call |

Two more facts:
- The Anthropic `none` field is good. On a prompt that tells the model to call a tool, Claude returned 200 with an **empty** message (one output token). On a neutral prompt it answered in text.
- The text history has a known cost. On the prompt that tells the model to call a tool, Nova and Sonnet both wrote fake call text, for example `[tool call t2: get_weather({"city": "Berlin"})]`. This is not a real tool call, but the user sees it as the answer.

**Approaches:**

1. **One fix for each family (my recommendation).** For `Anthropic`, send `toolConfig` with the user tools and the Anthropic `none` field. If the request has no user tools, also send a placeholder tool, because Converse needs at least one. For all other families, write the tool history as text and send no `toolConfig`. Every family then gets a 200 with no real tool call. Claude keeps the real tool structure. The cost: this adds `additionalModelRequestFields` to `PreparedConverse`, and it adds a text writer for tool blocks.
2. **Text history for every family.** This is one code path and needs no new request field. The cost: Claude loses the structured history, and Sonnet wrote fake call text in the probe while the `none` field gave a clean result.
3. **Anthropic `none` field, error for other families.** The fix is small and has no fake-text risk. The cost: a `None` turn after a tool loop then fails on Nova, Llama, Mistral and the other families. That is a smaller break than today's, but it is still a break.

In all three, a `None` request with no tool round in the history keeps today's shape: no tools and no `toolConfig`. The native path (`native.rs`) gets the same fix. The structured-output anchor case stays with SMA-847.

Which approach do you want? I recommend approach 1.

input.content:
# SMA-833: Bedrock `ToolChoice::None` with a tool history

## 1. Problem

When `model_settings.tool_choice` is `ToolChoice::None`, the Bedrock
translator sends no `toolConfig`. The forced-tool path does this in
`build_request` (`translate/mod.rs`, the `none_choice` early return). The
native path does it in `build_native` (`translate/native.rs`), because it
sends no user tools for `None`.

Converse requires `toolConfig` when the messages contain `toolUse` or
`toolResult` blocks. Thus a `None` turn after a tool loop fails with:

`ValidationException: The toolConfig field must be defined when using toolUse and toolResult content blocks.`

The usual case is a final "answer now, do not call tools" turn.

## 2. Required behavior

- A `None` request with a tool round in the history gets a 200 response.
- The model cannot make a real tool call in that turn.

## 3. Evidence (live probes, 2026-11-21, us-east-1)

The probes used the AWS CLI 2.39.6 and boto3 (`Converse` and
`ConverseStream`), with the `maip-dev-admin` profile. The history was one
`get_weather` round. The "adversarial" prompt told the model to call the tool
again. The "neutral" prompt asked for a summary.

| # | Request | Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 | Nova 2 Lite |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | No `toolConfig` (the current `None` shape) | 400, B15 error | 400, B15 error |
| P3 | `toolConfig.tools = []` | 400 `The provided request is not valid` (the CLI also refuses it, min length 1) | - |
| P2 | Tools, no `toolChoice` | 200, **real `toolUse`** | 200, **real `toolUse`** |
| P4 | Tools + `additionalModelRequestFields: {"tool_choice":{"type":"none"}}` | 200, no `toolUse`, on `Converse` and `ConverseStream` | 400 `extraneous key [tool_choice] is not permitted` |
| P5 | Only the `tool_choice` field, no `toolConfig` | 400, B15 error | - |
| P6 | Tool blocks written as text, no `toolConfig` | 200, no `toolUse` | 200, no `toolUse` |
| P7 | P4 with one placeholder tool instead of the history's tool | 200, but the model says that the earlier result "didn't come from a real weather tool" | - |
| P8 | P4 with a spec made from the history's tool name, schema `{"type":"object"}` | 200, no `toolUse`. Neutral: a correct answer | - |

Observations:

- P4 and P8, adversarial prompt: Claude returned 200 with an **empty**
  assistant message (one output token). Neutral prompt: a normal text answer.
- P6, adversarial prompt: Nova and Sonnet wrote fake call text, for example
  `[tool call t2: get_weather({"city": "Berlin"})]`. This is text, not a tool
  call. Opus wrote that it has no weather tool in this turn.
- P7 against P8: a placeholder tool makes Claude doubt the tool history. A
  spec with the history's real tool name does not.

Converse has no `none` value for `toolChoice` (only `auto`, `any`, `tool`).

## 4. Approaches

1. **One fix for each family (chosen by Sven, 2026-11-22).** Claude gets the
   Anthropic `tool_choice: none` field with a valid `toolConfig`. The other
   families get the tool history as text and no `toolConfig`. Every family
   gets a 200 with no real tool call, and Claude keeps the structured history.
2. **Text history for every family.** One code path and no new request field.
   Rejected: Claude loses the structured history, and P4 gives Claude a
   cleaner result than P6.
3. **Anthropic field, and an error for the other families.** Rejected: a
   `None` turn after a tool loop then still fails on all non-Claude families.

Rejected without a probe-backed alternative: tools with no `toolChoice` (P2),
because the model then calls a tool.

## 5. Design

### 5.1 When the fix applies

The fix applies only when both are true:

- `tool_choice` is `Some(ToolChoice::None)`, and
- the translated messages contain a `toolUse` or `toolResult` block (the
  existing `has_tool_round` test, moved to a place that both paths can use).

A `None` request with no tool round keeps today's shape: no tools, no
`toolConfig`, no new field. The existing test
`tool_choice_none_with_user_tools_omits_tool_config` stays green unchanged.

### 5.2 `ModelFamily::Anthropic`: the Anthropic `none` field

1. Build the tool list:
   - the user tools, through `tool_specs` (the same rewrite and the same
     reserved-name check as today), then
   - one derived spec for each tool name in the history's `toolUse` blocks
     that is not already in the list. The order is the first occurrence. Each
     derived spec has the name from the history, the description
     `A tool that this conversation used earlier.`, and the input schema
     `{"type":"object"}`. A derived spec skips the reserved-name check,
     because the name came from an earlier model turn (for example the
     synthesized structured-output tool).
2. If a `toolResult` block has no matching `toolUse` name (the history holds
   only results), no spec can be derived from it. If the list is then empty,
   add one placeholder spec named `__paigasus_tool_history__` with the
   description `Placeholder. Do not call this tool.` and the schema
   `{"type":"object"}`. Converse rejects an empty list (P3). This case is

| P5 | Only the `tool_choice` field, no `toolConfig` | 400, B15 error | - |
| P6 | Tool blocks written as text, no `toolConfig` | 200, no `toolUse` | 200, no `toolUse` |
| P7 | P4 with one placeholder tool instead of the history's tool | 200, but the model says that the earlier result "didn't come from a real weather tool" | - |
| P8 | P4 with a spec made from the history's tool name, schema `{"type":"object"}` | 200, no `toolUse`. Neutral: a correct answer | - |

  The per-family design is sound. The probes support it for the two native-path Claude models and Nova 2 Lite, and it keeps today's shape for `None` with no tool round. Three gaps need a fix before a plan is written. Section 5.4 silently reverses a SMA-839 ruling on a request shape that works today. Section 5.2 applies to every Claude model, but only the two native-path models were probed. The live test does not exercise the "no real tool call" requirement.
  
  ## Findings
  
  ### BLOCKER
  None.
  
  ### MAJOR
  
  - **5.4 reverses the SMA-839 anchor ruling for `None` + structured format + tool round, without saying so.**
    - What is wrong: Today the native path builds no user tools for `None` (`translate/native.rs:71-72`). It then adds the synthesized anchor when the format is structured and a tool round exists (`native.rs:88-93`). The SMA-839 spec rules this explicitly (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-21-sma-839-bedrock-native-structured-output-design.md:234,237`: "`outputConfig` only (and the anchor row applies)"). The existing test `snap_native_tool_choice_none_json_schema_finalizing_anchor` (`translate/mod.rs:1350-1365`) asserts `synthesizing == true` and tool names `[__paigasus_structured_output__]`. This shape gives a 200 today. Section 5.4 replaces it with `outputConfig` + derived specs + `tool_choice: none`, and none of the probes cover that combination: P4 and P8 sent no `outputConfig`. The spec names only `tool_choice_none_with_user_tools_omits_tool_config` as a test that stays unchanged. It does not say that this test and its `.snap` file must be inverted. `JsonObject` + `None` + tool round on the native path changes too: it loses the anchor and becomes plain text, and no test is listed for it.

    - Suggested fix: Choose one of two options. (a) Keep today's anchor for `structured && None && tool round` on the native path, and apply 5.2 only when the format is not structured. This is the simplest option, the request is already a 200, and the anchor is not a real tool. (b) Keep the change. Then add a live probe and a live test for `JsonSchema` + `None` + tool round on Sonnet 5.5. State the reversal of SMA-839 section 7.5 explicitly. List the inverted test, its snapshot and a new `JsonObject` case.
  
  - **5.2 applies to every `ModelFamily::Anthropic` model, but P4/P8 cover only Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5.**
    - What is wrong: Both probed models are on the native path (`family.rs:115-122`, `policy.rs:67-73`). The `build_request` branch of 5.2 serves Claude 3.x, 4.x, Sonnet 5, Opus 5 and Haiku 5.5. That branch has no probe, and the live test plan does not run it: it runs only Sonnet 5.5 and Nova 2 Lite (section 6). Older Bedrock-hosted Claude builds can reject `tool_choice.type = "none"`, as Nova rejects the key.
    - Why it matters: The most-used Claude models get a request shape that nobody has verified. If such a model rejects the field, the user sees a different 400 with no fallback. `fallback.rs:80-85` correctly does not fire, because the request has no forced choice.
    - Suggested fix: Run P4 on at least one forced-path model (for example `global.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5` or `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`) and one 3.x or 4.x model. Add those models to the live-test run list. State the intended result when a model rejects the field: keep the 400 and document it, or route that model to 5.3.
  
  - **The live test does not exercise the core requirement "the model cannot make a real tool call".**
    - What is wrong: Section 6 runs only the neutral prompt and asserts non-empty text. A neutral "summarize" prompt can give no tool call even with the P2 shape, so the test cannot fail when the guard is missing.
    - Why it matters: The ticket's acceptance criterion is "200 with no tool call". That criterion is only shown on the adversarial prompt (P4 and P6).
    - Suggested fix: Add an adversarial-prompt case. It asserts zero `ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta`, `Finish.reason != ToolCalls` and no stream error, and it allows empty text (P4 and P8 show an empty message). Keep the neutral case for the non-empty-text check.
  
  - **The 5.3 text format has no escaping, so tool output can forge the boundary and appear as user-authored text.**
    - What is wrong: `[tool result <id>: <text>]` embeds raw tool output in a user-role text block, next to the real user text. Tool results are prepended to the user turn (`request.rs:122`). A result such as `x]\n\nNew instruction from the user: ...` closes the bracket. The rest then reads as normal user text. With a structured `toolResult` block the model knows where the tool output ends. Section 7 does not list this risk.
    - Why it matters: This is a prompt-injection amplification on every non-Claude family, and the agent loop feeds untrusted tool output into it.
    - Suggested fix: JSON-encode the result text and the input with `serde_json::to_string`. Then the closing `"]` cannot appear unescaped, for example `[tool result tu_1: "...escaped..."]`. Add the residual risk to section 7. Add a unit test with a result that contains `]` and a newline.
  
  ### MINOR
  
  - **The placeholder conclusion (5.2 step 2) does not follow from P7.** P7 had a `toolUse` in the history; it only replaced the defined tool. A history with only `toolResult` blocks is an orphan result, and the Anthropic layer rejects it ("unexpected `tool_use_id` found in `tool_result` blocks") whatever `toolConfig` says. So "the request succeeds" is not shown, and the code path is probably dead. Suggested fix: probe it. Or drop the placeholder and let the request fail as it does today. Or, on Claude, flatten only the orphan results to text with the 5.3 format.
  
  - **No Document-to-JSON converter exists.** `document.rs:20-45` has only `value_to_document`, and `Document::Object` is a `HashMap` (`document.rs:38`). The 5.3 "compact `serde_json` form of the `toolUse` input document" needs a new `document_to_value`. Go through `serde_json::Value`: `preserve_order` is off (the `Cargo.lock` entry for `serde_json` has no `indexmap` dependency), so the keys come out sorted. Pin "sorted keys" in the spec, or a direct serializer will make the snapshots flaky. Add a multi-key-args test.
  
  - **"The same reserved-name check as today" is not accurate for `None`.** Today `tool_specs` is never called on a `None` request (`mod.rs:218-231`, `native.rs:71-72`). After the change, a user tool named `__paigasus_structured_output__` makes a `None` + tool-round request fail on Claude only. Decide whether that is intended, and add a test.
  
  - **The schema assertion cannot use the wire projection.** `to_wire_json` prints every input schema as `"<Document>"` (`mod.rs:430-433`). The tests for the `{"type":"object"}` derived schema must read the `ToolInputSchema` document directly. Also state whether the derived schema goes through `rewrite_tool_schema`. The synthesized `JsonObject` tool does (`response_format.rs:90-92`); 5.2 does not say.
  
  - **The "more than one text content block" case cannot occur.** `build_tool_result_block` always makes exactly one `Text` block (`request.rs:360-367`). Remove the case or mark it as defensive.
  
  - **The native-path "other families" branch (5.4) cannot be reached today.** The native path needs `from_model_id == Anthropic` (`family.rs:116`), and the learned flag needs `policy.family() == Anthropic` (`fallback.rs:80`). Say so, and test the branch through `build_native` directly, or omit it until SMA-837.
  
  - **Put the strategy on `ModelFamily` and use one helper.** Add for example `ModelFamily::tool_choice_none_strategy()`, next to `supports_forced_tool_choice` (`family.rs:94-96`). Use one shared helper that returns (messages, tools, extra fields) and call it from both builders. Without this, 5.2 and 5.3 get two copies that can drift. SMA-837 also gets one place to change.
  
  - **The field type.** A raw `Option<Document>` invites merge bugs when a later feature adds a second key, for example `thinking`, which the direct Anthropic provider already sends. Prefer a typed intent, such as `anthropic_tool_choice_none: bool`, and build the document in `send_converse_stream`. If you keep `Document`, define it as a merged JSON object.
  
  - **No local guard exists.** 5.2 relies on the service to honor `tool_choice: none`. On such a request `synthesizing == false`, so any `toolUse` becomes a `ToolCallDelta` (`stream.rs:139-147,193-197`) and the core executes it. Add a translator flag for `None` requests that turns a `ToolUse` start into `ModelError::Other`. It is cheap and unit-testable.
  
  - **Observability.** 5.3 changes the meaning of the request: the structured history becomes text. SMA-839 set the convention of one `warn!` per handle for each change of meaning (`policy.rs:86-102`). Add at least a `debug!`. If you add a notice kind, `warned: [AtomicBool; 3]` (`policy.rs:33`) must grow, and the "forced path leaves notices empty" doc (`mod.rs:48-50`) must change.
  
  - **A trailing `toolUse` with no result is not specified.** With 5.3 it becomes an assistant text that Converse treats as a prefill, so the model continues `[tool call ...`. With 5.2 the Anthropic layer rejects it. Define the intended result, for example a local error.
  
  - **The send wiring is not tested offline.** `.set_additional_model_request_fields` in `model.rs:49-60` is checked only by the live test. `output_config` has the same limit. Make the PR checklist require the live runs. Or capture the request body with the smithy test HTTP client.
  
  - **Docs.** The condition in section 8 is already true. `README.md:83` and `README.md:99` describe the native tool-choice mapping and must change. A search of `docs/book/src` found no tool-choice mapping page. Name these files in the spec.
  
  ### QUESTIONS
  
  - What does the core runner do with an empty assistant turn (the P4/P8 adversarial result: `Usage` + `Finish(Stop)` and no `TokenDelta`)? Is the final output `""`? Does an agent with an `output_type` then fail or start a repair turn? "Does not alter" does not tell a plan writer what users see.
  - If a Claude model rejects the `tool_choice` field, is a 400 acceptable, or should that handle switch to 5.3, similar to rule B?
  - Sessions can cross providers (`request.rs:139,198` drop foreign `ProviderData`). Can a history hold a tool name that fails the Converse `ToolSpecification` name pattern, for example a Gemini-style dotted name? If the `ToolUseBlock` name is not held to the same pattern, a derived spec makes a new 400. Should invalid names be skipped?
  - Does Sven approve the reversal of the SMA-839 section 7.5 anchor rows for `None`, or should that sub-case keep the anchor (see the first MAJOR finding)?
  
  ## What's good
  
  - Section 5.1 scopes the change tightly. A `None` request with no tool round stays byte-identical, and the request never sets a forced choice, so `send_with_fallback` cannot fire on it (`fallback.rs:67,80-85`).

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES
The per-family design is sound. The probes support it for the two native-path Claude models and Nova 2 Lite, and it keeps today's shape for `None` with no tool round. Three gaps need a fix before a plan is written. Section 5.4 silently reverses a SMA-839 ruling on a request shape that works today. Section 5.2 applies to every Claude model, but only the two native-path models were probed. The live test does not exercise the "no real tool call" requirement.

## Findings

### BLOCKER
None.

### MAJOR

- **5.4 reverses the SMA-839 anchor ruling for `None` + structured format + tool round, without saying so.**
  - What is wrong: Today the native path builds no user tools for `None` (`translate/native.rs:71-72`). It then adds the synthesized anchor when the format is structured and a tool round exists (`native.rs:88-93`). The SMA-839 spec rules this explicitly (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-21-sma-839-bedrock-native-structured-output-design.md:234,237`: "`outputConfig` only (and the anchor row applies)"). The existing test `snap_native_tool_choice_none_json_schema_finalizing_anchor` (`translate/mod.rs:1350-1365`) asserts `synthesizing == true` and tool names `[__paigasus_structured_output__]`. This shape gives a 200 today. Section 5.4 replaces it with `outputConfig` + derived specs + `tool_choice: none`, and none of the probes cover that combination: P4 and P8 sent no `outputConfig`. The spec names only `tool_choice_none_with_user_tools_omits_tool_config` as a test that stays unchanged. It does not say that this test and its `.snap` file must be inverted. `JsonObject` + `None` + tool round on the native path changes too: it loses the anchor and becomes plain text, and no test is listed for it.
  - Why it matters: A reviewed shape that works today becomes an unprobed shape. The plan writer will see a red test and must ask whether the reversal is intended. `README.md:83` ("the crate can add a hidden anchor tool") also becomes partly stale.
  - Suggested fix: Choose one of two options. (a) Keep today's anchor for `structured && None && tool round` on the native path, and apply 5.2 only when the format is not structured. This is the simplest option, the request is already a 200, and the anchor is not a real tool. (b) Keep the change. Then add a live probe and a live test for `JsonSchema` + `None` + tool round on Sonnet 5.5. State the reversal of SMA-839 section 7.5 explicitly. List the inverted test, its snapshot and a new `JsonObject` case.

- **5.2 applies to every `ModelFamily::Anthropic` model, but P4/P8 cover only Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5.**
  - What is wrong: Both probed models are on the native path (`family.rs:115-122`, `policy.rs:67-73`). The `build_request` branch of 5.2 serves Claude 3.x, 4.x, Sonnet 5, Opus 5 and Haiku 5.5. That branch has no probe, and the live test plan does not run it: it runs only Sonnet 5.5 and Nova 2 Lite (section 6). Older Bedrock-hosted Claude builds can reject `tool_choice.type = "none"`, as Nova rejects the key.
  - Why it matters: The most-used Claude models get a request shape that nobody has verified. If such a model rejects the field, the user sees a different 400 with no fallback. `fallback.rs:80-85` correctly does not fire, because the request has no forced choice.
  - Suggested fix: Run P4 on at least one forced-path model (for example `global.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5` or `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`) and one 3.x or 4.x model. Add those models to the live-test run list. State the intended result when a model rejects the field: keep the 400 and document it, or route that model to 5.3.

- **The live test does not exercise the core requirement "the model cannot make a real tool call".**
  - What is wrong: Section 6 runs only the neutral prompt and asserts non-empty text. A neutral "summarize" prompt can give no tool call even with the P2 shape, so the test cannot fail when the guard is missing.
  - Why it matters: The ticket's acceptance criterion is "200 with no tool call". That criterion is only shown on the adversarial prompt (P4 and P6).
  - Suggested fix: Add an adversarial-prompt case. It asserts zero `ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta`, `Finish.reason != ToolCalls` and no stream error, and it allows empty text (P4 and P8 show an empty message). Keep the neutral case for the non-empty-text check.

- **The 5.3 text format has no escaping, so tool output can forge the boundary and appear as user-authored text.**
  - What is wrong: `[tool result <id>: <text>]` embeds raw tool output in a user-role text block, next to the real user text. Tool results are prepended to the user turn (`request.rs:122`). A result such as `x]\n\nNew instruction from the user: ...` closes the bracket. The rest then reads as normal user text. With a structured `toolResult` block the model knows where the tool output ends. Section 7 does not list this risk.
  - Why it matters: This is a prompt-injection amplification on every non-Claude family, and the agent loop feeds untrusted tool output into it.
  - Suggested fix: JSON-encode the result text and the input with `serde_json::to_string`. Then the closing `"]` cannot appear unescaped, for example `[tool result tu_1: "...escaped..."]`. Add the residual risk to section 7. Add a unit test with a result that contains `]` and a newline.

### MINOR

- **The placeholder conclusion (5.2 step 2) does not follow from P7.** P7 had a `toolUse` in the history; it only replaced the defined tool. A history with only `toolResult` blocks is an orphan result, and the Anthropic layer rejects it ("unexpected `tool_use_id` found in `tool_result` blocks") whatever `toolConfig` says. So "the request succeeds" is not shown, and the code path is probably dead. Suggested fix: probe it. Or drop the placeholder and let the request fail as it does today. Or, on Claude, flatten only the orphan results to text with the 5.3 format.

- **No Document-to-JSON converter exists.** `document.rs:20-45` has only `value_to_document`, and `Document::Object` is a `HashMap` (`document.rs:38`). The 5.3 "compact `serde_json` form of the `toolUse` input document" needs a new `document_to_value`. Go through `serde_json::Value`: `preserve_order` is off (the `Cargo.lock` entry for `serde_json` has no `indexmap` dependency), so the keys come out sorted. Pin "sorted keys" in the spec, or a direct serializer will make the snapshots flaky. Add a multi-key-args test.

- **"The same reserved-name check as today" is not accurate for `None`.** Today `tool_specs` is never called on a `None` request (`mod.rs:218-231`, `native.rs:71-72`). After the change, a user tool named `__paigasus_structured_output__` makes a `None` + tool-round request fail on Claude only. Decide whether that is intended, and add a test.

- **The schema assertion cannot use the wire projection.** `to_wire_json` prints every input schema as `"<Document>"` (`mod.rs:430-433`). The tests for the `{"type":"object"}` derived schema must read the `ToolInputSchema` document directly. Also state whether the derived schema goes through `rewrite_tool_schema`. The synthesized `JsonObject` tool does (`response_format.rs:90-92`); 5.2 does not say.

- **The "more than one text content block" case cannot occur.** `build_tool_result_block` always makes exactly one `Text` block (`request.rs:360-367`). Remove the case or mark it as defensive.

- **The native-path "other families" branch (5.4) cannot be reached today.** The native path needs `from_model_id == Anthropic` (`family.rs:116`), and the learned flag needs `policy.family() == Anthropic` (`fallback.rs:80`). Say so, and test the branch through `build_native` directly, or omit it until SMA-837.

- **Put the strategy on `ModelFamily` and use one helper.** Add for example `ModelFamily::tool_choice_none_strategy()`, next to `supports_forced_tool_choice` (`family.rs:94-96`). Use one shared helper that returns (messages, tools, extra fields) and call it from both builders. Without this, 5.2 and 5.3 get two copies that can drift. SMA-837 also gets one place to change.

- **The field type.** A raw `Option<Document>` invites merge bugs when a later feature adds a second key, for example `thinking`, which the direct Anthropic provider already sends. Prefer a typed intent, such as `anthropic_tool_choice_none: bool`, and build the document in `send_converse_stream`. If you keep `Document`, define it as a merged JSON object.

- **No local guard exists.** 5.2 relies on the service to honor `tool_choice: none`. On such a request `synthesizing == false`, so any `toolUse` becomes a `ToolCallDelta` (`stream.rs:139-147,193-197`) and the core executes it. Add a translator flag for `None` requests that turns a `ToolUse` start into `ModelError::Other`. It is cheap and unit-testable.

- **Observability.** 5.3 changes the meaning of the request: the structured history becomes text. SMA-839 set the convention of one `warn!` per handle for each change of meaning (`policy.rs:86-102`). Add at least a `debug!`. If you add a notice kind, `warned: [AtomicBool; 3]` (`policy.rs:33`) must grow, and the "forced path leaves notices empty" doc (`mod.rs:48-50`) must change.

- **A trailing `toolUse` with no result is not specified.** With 5.3 it becomes an assistant text that Converse treats as a prefill, so the model continues `[tool call ...`. With 5.2 the Anthropic layer rejects it. Define the intended result, for example a local error.

- **The send wiring is not tested offline.** `.set_additional_model_request_fields` in `model.rs:49-60` is checked only by the live test. `output_config` has the same limit. Make the PR checklist require the live runs. Or capture the request body with the smithy test HTTP client.

- **Docs.** The condition in section 8 is already true. `README.md:83` and `README.md:99` describe the native tool-choice mapping and must change. A search of `docs/book/src` found no tool-choice mapping page. Name these files in the spec.

### QUESTIONS

- What does the core runner do with an empty assistant turn (the P4/P8 adversarial result: `Usage` + `Finish(Stop)` and no `TokenDelta`)? Is the final output `""`? Does an agent with an `output_type` then fail or start a repair turn? "Does not alter" does not tell a plan writer what users see.
- If a Claude model rejects the `tool_choice` field, is a 400 acceptable, or should that handle switch to 5.3, similar to rule B?
- Sessions can cross providers (`request.rs:139,198` drop foreign `ProviderData`). Can a history hold a tool name that fails the Converse `ToolSpecification` name pattern, for example a Gemini-style dotted name? If the `ToolUseBlock` name is not held to the same pattern, a derived spec makes a new 400. Should invalid names be skipped?

## What's good

- 5.3 is a post-pass over the translated `ContentBlock`s, not a rewrite of the core `Item`s. This keeps the role-alternation and round-coalescing rules of `items_to_messages` (`round_is_answered`, the all-`ToolUse` check at `request.rs:215-218`) out of the change.
- The evidence section is concrete and honest. It records the costs (the empty Claude answer, the fake call text) and the unprobed families, and it uses the history's real tool names because P7 showed that a placeholder lowers the answer quality.

# SMA-833: Bedrock `ToolChoice::None` with a tool history

## 1. Problem

When `model_settings.tool_choice` is `ToolChoice::None`, the Bedrock
translator sends no `toolConfig`. The forced-tool path does this in
`build_request` (`translate/mod.rs`, the `none_choice` early return). The
native path does it in `build_native` (`translate/native.rs:70-76`), because
it sends no user tools for `None`.

Converse requires `toolConfig` when the messages contain `toolUse` or
`toolResult` blocks. Thus a `None` turn after a tool loop fails with:

`ValidationException: The toolConfig field must be defined when using toolUse and toolResult content blocks.`

The usual case is a final "answer now, do not call tools" turn.

## 2. Required behavior

- A `None` request with a tool round in the history gets a 200 response.
- The model cannot make a real tool call in that turn.

## 3. Evidence (live probes, 2026-11-21 and 2026-11-22, us-east-1)

The probes used the AWS CLI 2.39.6 and boto3 (`Converse` and
`ConverseStream`), with the `maip-dev-admin` profile. The history was one
`get_weather` round. The "adversarial" prompt told the model to call the tool
again. The "neutral" prompt asked for a summary.

| # | Request | Result |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | No `toolConfig` (the current `None` shape) | Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Nova 2 Lite: 400, B15 error |
| P2 | Tools, no `toolChoice` | Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Nova 2 Lite: 200, **real `toolUse`** |
| P3 | `toolConfig.tools = []` | Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5: 400 `The provided request is not valid` (the CLI also refuses it, min length 1) |
| P4 | Tools + `additionalModelRequestFields: {"tool_choice":{"type":"none"}}` | Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5: 200, no `toolUse`, on `Converse` and `ConverseStream`. Nova 2 Lite: 400 `extraneous key [tool_choice] is not permitted` |
| P5 | Only the `tool_choice` field, no `toolConfig` | Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5: 400, B15 error |
| P6 | Tool blocks written as text, no `toolConfig` | Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Nova 2 Lite: 200, no `toolUse` |
| P7 | P4 with one placeholder tool instead of the history's tool | Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5: 200, but the model says that the earlier result "didn't come from a real weather tool" |
| P8 | P4 with a spec made from the history's tool name, schema `{"type":"object"}` | Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5: 200, no `toolUse`. Neutral: a correct answer |
| P9 | P8 on forced-tool-path Claude models | Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5, Opus 5, Sonnet 4.5: 200, no `toolUse`, on `Converse` and `ConverseStream`. Neutral: a correct answer. Claude 3.5 Haiku and 3.7 Sonnet: end of life on Bedrock (`ResourceNotFoundException`), not testable |
| P10 | A history with only a `toolResult` (no `toolUse`), placeholder tool, P4 field | Sonnet 5.5: 400 `Expected toolResult blocks at messages.0.content for the following Ids: t1` |

Observations:

- P4, P8, P9, adversarial prompt: Claude returned 200 with an **empty**
  assistant message (one output token, sometimes one empty reasoning block).
  Neutral prompt: a normal text answer.
- P6, adversarial prompt: Nova and Sonnet wrote fake call text, for example
  `[tool call t2: get_weather({"city": "Berlin"})]`. This is text, not a tool
  call. Opus wrote that it has no weather tool in this turn.
- P7 against P8: a placeholder tool makes Claude doubt the tool history. A
  spec with the history's real tool name does not.
- P10: Converse rejects an orphan tool result, whatever the `toolConfig` holds.

Converse has no `none` value for `toolChoice` (only `auto`, `any`, `tool`).

## 4. Approaches

1. **One fix for each family (chosen by Sven, 2026-11-22).** Claude gets the
   Anthropic `tool_choice: none` field with a valid `toolConfig`. The other
   families get the tool history as text and no `toolConfig`. Every family
   gets a 200 with no real tool call, and Claude keeps the structured history.
2. **Text history for every family.** One code path and no new request field.
   Rejected: Claude loses the structured history, and P4 gives Claude a
   cleaner result than P6.
3. **Anthropic field, and an error for the other families.** Rejected: a
   `None` turn after a tool loop then still fails on all non-Claude families.

Rejected without a probe-backed alternative: tools with no `toolChoice` (P2),
because the model then calls a tool.

## 5. Design

### 5.1 When the fix applies

The fix applies only when all of these are true:

- `tool_choice` is `Some(ToolChoice::None)`,
- the translated messages contain a `toolUse` or `toolResult` block (the
  existing `has_tool_round` test, moved to a place that both paths can use),
  and
- on the native path, the response format is not `JsonSchema` or
  `JsonObject` (see 5.5).

A `None` request with no tool round keeps today's shape: no tools, no
`toolConfig`, no new field. The existing test
`tool_choice_none_with_user_tools_omits_tool_config` stays green unchanged.

### 5.2 The strategy lives on `ModelFamily`

Add `ModelFamily::tool_choice_none_strategy() -> ToolChoiceNoneStrategy`
next to `supports_forced_tool_choice` (`family.rs`). It is `pub(crate)`.

`ValidationException: The toolConfig field must be defined when using toolUse and toolResult content blocks.`

The usual case is a final "answer now, do not call tools" turn.

## 2. Required behavior

- A `None` request with a tool round in the history gets a 200 response.
- The model cannot make a real tool call in that turn.

## 3. Evidence (live probes, 2026-11-21 and 2026-11-22, us-east-1)

The probes used the AWS CLI 2.39.6 and boto3 (`Converse` and

again. The "neutral" prompt asked for a summary.

`toolResult` blocks. Thus a `None` turn after a tool loop fails with:

`ValidationException: The toolConfig field must be defined when using toolUse and toolResult content blocks.`

The usual case is a final "answer now, do not call tools" turn.

## 2. Required behavior

- A `None` request with a tool round in the history gets a 200 response.
- The model cannot make a real tool call in that turn.

## 3. Evidence (live probes, 2026-11-21 and 2026-11-22, us-east-1)

The probes used the AWS CLI 2.39.6 and boto3 (`Converse` and
`ConverseStream`), with the `maip-dev-admin` profile. The history was one
`get_weather` round. The "adversarial" prompt told the model to call the tool
again. The "neutral" prompt asked for a summary.

| # | Request | Result |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | No `toolConfig` (the current `None` shape) | Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Nova 2 Lite: 400, B15 error |
| P2 | Tools, no `toolChoice` | Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Nova 2 Lite: 200, **real `toolUse`** |
| P3 | `toolConfig.tools = []` | Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5: 400 `The provided request is not valid` (the CLI also refuses it, min length 1) |
| P4 | Tools + `additionalModelRequestFields: {"tool_choice":{"type":"none"}}` | Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5: 200, no `toolUse`, on `Converse` and `ConverseStream`. Nova 2 Lite: 400 `extraneous key [tool_choice] is not permitted` |
| P5 | Only the `tool_choice` field, no `toolConfig` | Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5: 400, B15 error |
| P6 | Tool blocks written as text, no `toolConfig` | Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Nova 2 Lite: 200, no `toolUse` |
| P7 | P4 with one placeholder tool instead of the history's tool | Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5: 200, but the model says that the earlier result "didn't come from a real weather tool" |
| P8 | P4 with a spec made from the history's tool name, schema `{"type":"object"}` | Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5: 200, no `toolUse`. Neutral: a correct answer |
| P9 | P8 on forced-tool-path Claude models | Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5, Opus 5, Sonnet 4.5: 200, no `toolUse`, on `Converse` and `ConverseStream`. Neutral: a correct answer. Claude 3.5 Haiku and 3.7 Sonnet: end of life on Bedrock (`ResourceNotFoundException`), not testable |
| P10 | A history with only a `toolResult` (no `toolUse`), placeholder tool, P4 field | Sonnet 5.5: 400 `Expected toolResult blocks at messages.0.content for the following Ids: t1` |

Observations:

- P4, P8, P9, adversarial prompt: Claude returned 200 with an **empty**
  assistant message (one output token, sometimes one empty reasoning block).
  Neutral prompt: a normal text answer.
- P6, adversarial prompt: Nova and Sonnet wrote fake call text, for example
  `[tool call t2: get_weather({"city": "Berlin"})]`. This is text, not a tool
  call. Opus wrote that it has no weather tool in this turn.
- P7 against P8: a placeholder tool makes Claude doubt the tool history. A
  spec with the history's real tool name does not.
- P10: Converse rejects an orphan tool result, whatever the `toolConfig` holds.

Converse has no `none` value for `toolChoice` (only `auto`, `any`, `tool`).

## 4. Approaches

1. **One fix for each family (chosen by Sven, 2026-11-22).** Claude gets the
   Anthropic `tool_choice: none` field with a valid `toolConfig`. The other
   families get the tool history as text and no `toolConfig`. Every family
   gets a 200 with no real tool call, and Claude keeps the structured history.
2. **Text history for every family.** One code path and no new request field.
   Rejected: Claude loses the structured history, and P4 gives Claude a
   cleaner result than P6.
3. **Anthropic field, and an error for the other families.** Rejected: a
   `None` turn after a tool loop then still fails on all non-Claude families.

Rejected without a probe-backed alternative: tools with no `toolChoice` (P2),
because the model then calls a tool.

## 5. Design

### 5.1 When the fix applies

The fix applies only when all of these are true:

- `tool_choice` is `Some(ToolChoice::None)`,
- the translated messages contain a `toolUse` or `toolResult` block (the
  existing `has_tool_round` test, moved to a place that both paths can use),
  and
- on the native path, the response format is not `JsonSchema` or
  `JsonObject` (see 5.5).

A `None` request with no tool round keeps today's shape: no tools, no
`toolConfig`, no new field. The existing test
`tool_choice_none_with_user_tools_omits_tool_config` stays green unchanged.

### 5.2 The strategy lives on `ModelFamily`

Add `ModelFamily::tool_choice_none_strategy() -> ToolChoiceNoneStrategy`
next to `supports_forced_tool_choice` (`family.rs`). It is `pub(crate)`.

- `Anthropic` → `ToolChoiceNoneStrategy::AnthropicNoneField` (5.3).
- `AmazonNova`, `AmazonTitan`, `Llama`, `Mistral`, `Cohere`, `Unknown` →
  `ToolChoiceNoneStrategy::TextHistory` (5.4).

One shared helper in the `translate` module applies the strategy. It takes the
translated messages, the user tools, the family and the ruleset. It returns
the final messages, the tool list and the `tool_choice_none` flag (5.3 step
4). Both builders call this helper, so the two paths cannot drift. SMA-837 (a
family override) then changes the branch through the family only.

### 5.3 `AnthropicNoneField` (Claude)

1. Build the tool list:
   - the user tools, through `tool_specs` (the same schema rewrite and the
     same reserved-name check that every other tool choice uses), then
   - one derived spec for each tool name in the history's `toolUse` blocks
     that is not already in the list. The order is the first occurrence, with
     no duplicates. Each derived spec has the name from the history, the
     description `A tool that this conversation used earlier.`, and the input
     schema `{"type":"object"}`. This schema does not go through
     `rewrite_tool_schema`; it has nothing to rewrite. A derived spec skips
     the reserved-name check, because the name came from an earlier model
     turn (for example the synthesized structured-output tool). A name that
     the `ToolSpecification` builder refuses is skipped with a `debug!`; a
     `toolUse` with no matching spec is accepted (P7 has one).
2. If the list is empty after step 1, the helper changes nothing: the request
   keeps today's shape. This occurs only for a history with orphan tool
   results and no user tools, and Converse rejects that history anyway (P10).
   No placeholder tool is added.
3. Send `toolConfig` with this list and **no** `toolChoice`.
4. Set the new `PreparedConverse` field `tool_choice_none: bool` to `true`.
   `send_converse_stream` (`model.rs`) then sends
   `additionalModelRequestFields = {"tool_choice": {"type": "none"}}`. The
   flag is a typed intent and not a raw `Document`, so a later feature that
   adds a second key (for example `thinking`) merges into one JSON object at
   one place. All other builders set the flag to `false`. The
   wire-projection helper for the snapshot tests prints the field when the
   flag is set.

A user tool named `__paigasus_structured_output__` now makes a `None` request
with a tool round fail on Claude with the existing reserved-name error. This
is the same error that every other tool choice gives, so it is intended.

`has_forced_tool_choice()` stays `false` for this request, so the
forced-choice fallback (`fallback.rs`) never fires for it.

### 5.4 `TextHistory` (all other families)

Nova rejects the Anthropic field (P4), and we have no evidence that the other
families accept it.

After `items_to_messages`, replace every tool block in the messages:

- `ContentBlock::ToolUse` becomes
  `ContentBlock::Text("[tool call <toolUseId>: <name> <input>]")`.
- `ContentBlock::ToolResult` becomes
  `ContentBlock::Text("[tool result <toolUseId>: <text>]")`.

`<input>` and `<text>` are JSON-encoded with `serde_json::to_string`. The
input goes from the `Document` to a `serde_json::Value` through a new
`document_to_value` helper in `document.rs`. The workspace builds
`serde_json` without `preserve_order`, so object keys come out **sorted**, and
the text is stable. `<text>` is the JSON string literal of the result text, so
a result that holds `]`, a quote or a newline cannot close the bracket early.
The translator makes exactly one text content block per tool result today
(`build_tool_result_block`). The helper joins the text of all text blocks with
`\n` only as a defensive case.

The order of the blocks in each message does not change. The request sends no
`toolConfig` and the flag stays `false`. The helper logs one `debug!` with
target `paigasus::bedrock::translate` when it writes a history as text.

### 5.5 Both wire paths

- **Forced-tool path (`build_request`).** The `none_choice` early return calls
  the helper when 5.1 is true. The existing conflict guard (`JsonSchema` or
  `JsonObject` with `None`, on families that support forced tool choice) does
  not change and runs first.
- **Native path (`build_native`).** When the format is not structured, `None`
  with a tool round calls the helper. When the format is `JsonSchema` or
  `JsonObject`, the path keeps today's shape: no user tools and the hidden
  anchor (SMA-839 section 7.5). That shape is a 200 today, and the test
  `snap_native_tool_choice_none_json_schema_finalizing_anchor` stays
  unchanged. That the model can call the anchor is SMA-847.
- The native path is used only for `ModelFamily::Anthropic` today
  (`family.rs`, `fallback.rs`), so its `TextHistory` branch is not reachable
  yet. It goes through the shared helper and gets a unit test that calls
  `build_native` with a Nova config directly.

### 5.6 A local guard in the stream translator

Do not rely only on the service to honor `tool_choice: none`. When the
request has `tool_choice == Some(ToolChoice::None)` (any family), the stream
translator turns a `toolUse` content block start into
`ModelError::Other("the model called a tool, but tool_choice is None")` and
emits no `ToolCallDelta` for it. The translator gets this as one more input
flag, set from the `ModelRequest` when the stream starts. A synthesized anchor
call (the native `JsonSchema` + `None` case of 5.5) is not a user tool call:
the guard does not fire while `synthesizing` is `true`.

## 7. Known limits and non-goals

- **Empty answer on Claude.** When the prompt tells Claude to call a tool and
  the `none` field forbids it, Claude can return an empty message (P4, P8,
  P9). The request succeeds and makes no tool call, which meets the ticket.
  This change does not alter how the core runner handles an empty assistant
  turn; the plan does not investigate it. If it causes a problem, that is a
  new Linear issue.
- **Fake call text on other families** (5.4, P6). The model can write text in
  the `[tool call ...]` format. It is never a real tool call.
- **Prompt injection through the text history.** On the `TextHistory`
  families, the tool result sits in a user-role text block. JSON encoding
  stops a result from closing the bracket, but the model can still read
  instructions inside the result as user text more easily than inside a
  structured `toolResult` block.
- **No probe for Titan, Llama, Mistral, Cohere.** They get 5.4 because it
  sends no tool fields at all, so it does not depend on what each family
  accepts.
- **Claude 3.x is not probed** (end of life on Bedrock). If a Claude model
  rejects the `tool_choice` field, the request fails with that 400. There is
  no automatic change to 5.4.
- **A history that ends with an unanswered `toolUse`** behaves as today in
  `items_to_messages`. This change adds no new check for it.
- The native anchor case (`JsonSchema` or `JsonObject` with `None`) is
  SMA-847.
- A `ModelFamily` override (SMA-837) changes which strategy a model gets
  through 5.2, and needs no work here.

## GATE 1: spec approval

I revised the spec at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-22-sma-833-bedrock-tool-choice-none-design.md`, and it is ready for your approval.

**The design (approach 1):**
- **Claude:** for `ToolChoice::None` with a tool round in the history, the request sends a `toolConfig` and `additionalModelRequestFields: {"tool_choice":{"type":"none"}}`. The `toolConfig` holds the user tools plus a spec for each tool name in the history.
- **All other families:** the tool blocks become JSON-escaped text, and the request has no `toolConfig`.
- **No tool round:** the request keeps today's shape.

**Challenger verdict:** "approve with changes". It found no blockers, 4 major findings, 12 minor findings and 4 questions.

**Changes I made from the findings:**
- **Native structured output with `None`:** this case keeps today's shape (the hidden anchor tool). The change would have silently reversed a SMA-839 ruling on a request that works today. The anchor stays with SMA-847.
- **Forced-tool-path Claude models:** I probed them. Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5, Opus 5 and Sonnet 4.5 all accept the `none` field and make no tool call. I could not test Claude 3.5 or 3.7, because Bedrock has ended those models. A Claude model that rejects the field fails with its 400, and the spec records this.
- **Live tests:** I added a case with a prompt that tells the model to call a tool. It asserts that no tool call is made. The live tests run on Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Nova 2 Lite.
- **Text history:** the tool input and the tool result text are JSON-encoded, so a tool result cannot close the bracket and pose as user text. The prompt-injection risk that remains is in section 7.
- **Placeholder tool:** I removed it. A history with only a `toolResult` fails on Converse whatever `toolConfig` holds (probe P10), so the placeholder could never help.
- **Structure:** the strategy is on `ModelFamily`, and one shared helper serves both paths. The new request field is a typed `tool_choice_none: bool`, not a raw `Document`. Keys come out sorted through a new `document_to_value` helper.
- **Local guard:** the stream translator turns a real tool call on a `None` request into an error.
- **Smaller items:**
  - A `debug!` log line for the text history.
  - The README is named at lines 83 and 99. There is no book page on this topic.
  - Specific tests for reserved names, repeated names and the native branch for non-Claude families. That branch is not reachable today.

**Findings I did not act on:**
- **Empty Claude answer:** the core's handling of an empty turn is recorded as a known limit. If it causes a problem, it becomes a new Linear issue.
- **A history that ends with an unanswered `toolUse`:** the behavior does not change. This is outside the ticket.
- **An offline test for the send wiring:** I use the live runs instead, which is the same approach as for `output_config`. The PR does not open before those runs pass.

**One item needs your decision.** I added the local stream guard in section 5.6. If you consider it scope creep, I can remove it.

Do you approve, want changes, or want another challenge run?

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write implementation plans for an engineer who has not seen this codebase or this spec. Assume they write idiomatic code in the project's language once they know the exact interface and the exact test, and that they will make a reasonable choice wherever the plan leaves one open. What they cannot know is what you decided: which files, which names and signatures, which values from the spec, which tests prove each task. Document those. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Step Granularity

**Each step is one action with a checkable result:**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

**Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements — the plan
argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

## Review Focus

[The five input classes or failure modes the spec implies but no task's
tests exercise that are most likely to bite a person using this software
— one line each, naming the input or condition and the behavior a
reasonable person would expect, most likely first. The spec is a vision
document: it says what the software must do, not everything it will
meet, and its silence on an input is not permission for that input to
break the program. Write the list here, once, with the spec in front of
you. Then, for each line, add the test that pins it to the task that
owns the code, in that task's own step style.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
- Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter
  and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this
  block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `function(input: InputType) -> ResultType` in `exact/path/to/file.py`**

One line on the approach when the signature and the test leave a choice
(which library call, which data structure); a code block only for an
algorithm they do not determine.

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## What a Step Contains

A step is done when the implementer can write exactly one reasonable thing
from it. That is the whole requirement: unambiguous, not complete. Each kind
of step carries what makes it unambiguous and nothing more:

- **A test step:** the test's name and its assertions, as code, with the
  spec's exact values in them.
- **A code step:** the exact signature (name, parameters, return type), the
  file it lives in, and the specific values the spec pins. The implementer
  writes the body. A body appears only for an algorithm the signature and
  tests do not determine, or for exact copy the spec fixes.
- **A verification step:** the command to run and the output that means it
  passed.
- **A reference to another task:** that task's Interfaces block says what
  to use; the plan does not repeat that task's code.

A plan is the set of decisions the implementer cannot make alone. A plan
longer than the code it describes has written the code instead. Lines that
decide nothing ("TBD", "handle edge cases", "add appropriate validation",
"write tests for the above", a type or function no task defines) are the
opposite failure, and the self-review catches both.

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Step scan:** Every step must let the implementer write exactly one reasonable thing, and no step may carry more than that: a line that decides nothing is a gap, a function body the signature and tests already determine is a transcript. Fix both.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

**4. Review Focus:** For each input class or failure mode the spec implies, is there a task whose tests exercise it? The five uncovered ones most likely to bite a person go in the Review Focus section, and each line there gets its test added to the owning task. An empty section means you checked and found none, not that you skipped the check.

**5. Proportion:** Compare the plan's length to the spec's. A plan several times longer than the spec it implements is a transcript of the program, not a plan. If code blocks are most of the document, replace bodies with signatures, test names and assertions, and check that each step is still unambiguous.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving and self-reviewing the plan, link it for your human partner
to read. If they have already explicitly supplied an execution method, ask
them to review the plan and confirm it captures what they want; wait for that
review before implementation, then use the preserved method. Otherwise, ask
them to review the plan and choose an execution method before implementation.

**When no execution method has already been supplied:**

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Which execution approach would you prefer?**

- **Subagent-driven** - A fresh subagent implements each task and a fresh reviewer checks it before the next one starts, then a whole-branch review at the end. Most thorough; costs a fresh context per task and per review.
- **Native** - I implement every task myself in this session, the way this harness runs work, then one fresh reviewer on the most capable model checks the whole branch. Cheapest and fastest; no independent review until the end. Runs well with a mid-tier session model, since the plan carries the design.

**For this plan I recommend <one of the two>, because <one sentence from the plan: how much the tasks depend on each other's interfaces, how many there are, what a shipped mistake would cost>. Does the plan capture what you want, and which approach should we use?"**

**When an execution method has already been supplied:**

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Does it capture what you want?"**

**If Subagent-driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development

**If Native chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans

# SMA-833 Bedrock `ToolChoice::None` with a tool history: implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** A Bedrock request with `ToolChoice::None` and a tool round in the history gets a 200 response, and the model cannot make a real tool call.

**Architecture:** One new translate module applies a per-family strategy after `items_to_messages`. Claude gets derived tool specs plus a typed flag that `model.rs` turns into `additionalModelRequestFields = {"tool_choice":{"type":"none"}}`. All other families get their tool blocks written as JSON-escaped text. A stream-translator guard turns any real tool call on a `None` request into an error.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 1.94, `aws-sdk-bedrockruntime`, `aws-smithy-types::Document`, `serde_json` (no `preserve_order`), `insta` snapshots.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-22-sma-833-bedrock-tool-choice-none-design.md`

## Global Constraints

- Crate: `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock`. No other crate changes. No public API changes; every new item is `pub(crate)`.
- Commit format: `<type>(providers): SMA-833 <lowercase subject>`, with the trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Use `fix(providers)` for code and `test(providers)` / `docs(providers)` where it fits.
- Derived spec description, exact: `A tool that this conversation used earlier.` Derived schema, exact: `{"type":"object"}`.
- Text formats, exact: `[tool call <toolUseId>: <name> <input JSON>]` and `[tool result <toolUseId>: <JSON string of the text>]`.
- Extra request field, exact: `{"tool_choice": {"type": "none"}}`.
- Stream guard error text, exact: `the model called a tool, but tool_choice is None`.
- Log target: `paigasus::bedrock::translate`.
- Run `cargo fmt --all` and `cargo clippy -p paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` before each commit.
- Work in the foreground. Do not end a task while a cargo command still runs.
- Do not run `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git reset`, `git stash` or `git merge`. Stay on `feature/sma-833-bedrock-toolchoicenone-sends-no-toolconfig` in `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-833`. Stage files with explicit paths, never `git add -A`.

## Review Focus

1. A history that calls two different tools and one tool twice: Claude gets each name once, in first-occurrence order. Pinned in Task 3 (`claude_derives_each_name_once_in_order`).
2. A tool input with nested objects and several keys: the text history must be byte-stable across runs (sorted keys). Pinned in Task 1 and Task 3 (`text_history_sorts_input_keys`).
3. A tool result that holds `]`, `"` and a newline: it must not close the bracket. Pinned in Task 3 (`text_history_escapes_result_text`).
4. A `None` request on the forced path that later falls back to the native path (rule B): both builds must give the same `None` shape. Pinned in Task 4 (`none_shape_is_the_same_on_both_paths`).
5. A request with `None` and no tool round: its wire shape must not change. Pinned in Task 4 by the existing snapshot `snap_tool_choice_none_with_user_tools_omits_tool_config` (it must stay unchanged) and `none_without_tool_round_keeps_shape_on_nova`.

### Task 3: the `tool_choice_none` translate module

# SMA-833 Bedrock `ToolChoice::None` with a tool history: implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** A Bedrock request with `ToolChoice::None` and a tool round in the history gets a 200 response, and the model cannot make a real tool call.

**Architecture:** One new translate module applies a per-family strategy after `items_to_messages`. Claude gets derived tool specs plus a typed flag that `model.rs` turns into `additionalModelRequestFields = {"tool_choice":{"type":"none"}}`. All other families get their tool blocks written as JSON-escaped text. A stream-translator guard turns any real tool call on a `None` request into an error.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-22-sma-833-bedrock-tool-choice-none-design.md`

The result text is all `ToolResultContentBlock::Text` contents joined with `\n`, then `serde_json::to_string` of that string. `tools` empty, flag `false`. Log one `debug!` when at least one block changed.

# SMA-833 Bedrock `ToolChoice::None` with a tool history: implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** A Bedrock request with `ToolChoice::None` and a tool round in the history gets a 200 response, and the model cannot make a real tool call.

**Architecture:** One new translate module applies a per-family strategy after `items_to_messages`. Claude gets derived tool specs plus a typed flag that `model.rs` turns into `additionalModelRequestFields = {"tool_choice":{"type":"none"}}`. All other families get their tool blocks written as JSON-escaped text. A stream-translator guard turns any real tool call on a `None` request into an error.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 1.94, `aws-sdk-bedrockruntime`, `aws-smithy-types::Document`, `serde_json` (no `preserve_order`), `insta` snapshots.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-22-sma-833-bedrock-tool-choice-none-design.md`
